newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA C.BANK TAKES OVER MOLLOVBANK FOR 3 MONTHS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA C.BANK TAKES OVER MOLLOVBANK FOR 3 MONTHS.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) decided to put under direct administration the private Mollovbank, in receivership since September 23, in a bid to save it from bankruptcy, the State Gazette said on Friday.

"The BNB board decided to take over the powers of Mollovbank general shareholders' meeting for three months to create possibilities for its rehabilitation and avoid insolvency," the State Gazette said.

The BNB put Mollovbank in receivership, dismissed its management and appointed sequestrators on September 23 due to a danger of insolvency, citing a negative capital-to-risk assets ratio of 19 percent and oustanding payments of 22 million levs.
On October 31 the BNB filed a bankruptcy suit against Mollovbank, saying the bank's performing assets were not large enough to cover its liabilities.
Under BNB regulations sequestrators have managed the current affairs of a bank in receivership but its shareholders have retained their voting rights.

"Taking over the powers (of the shareholders meeting) could be seen as a step towards a possible Mollovbank's acquisition by a foreign investor expected to contribute to a capital rise with fresh money," a BNB official who declined to be named told Reuters.
The BNB was expected next week to announce a capital rise for the bank, the official said, declining to elaborate.
Mollovbank's registered share capital amounts to 1.4 billion levs, the minumum required for a domestic licence at present but figures of the effectively paid-in capital are not available.
If the BNB estimated the expected investment large enough to boost Mollovbank's liquidity and cover its capital gap it might be willing to consider lifting the receivership, the official said.
Since last May the BNB has filed insolvency suits against sixteen state and private banks, a third of Bulgaria's banks.
Only Madan-based Krystalbank, which stopped operating in November 1995, has been declared insolvent by the court so far. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
